p: The purpose of this epistle, is to show that Jesus Christ the Son of God both God and man is that true eternal and only Prophet, King and High Priest, that was shadowed by the figures of the old law, and is now indeed exhibited of whom the whole Church ought to be taught, governed and sanctified.

sundry times and in divers manners: The first part of the general proposition of this epistle the son of God is indeed that prophet or teacher, who has actually now performed that which God after a sort and in shadows signified by his prophets, and has fully revealed his Father's will to the world.
last days spoken unto us by: So that the former declaration made by the prophets was not complete, and nothing must be added to this latter.
Son: That one Son is God and man.

whom he hath appointed: The second part of the same statement: The same Son is appointed by the Father to be our king and Lord, by whom also he made all things: and in whom only he sets forth his glory, yea and himself also to be under obligation to us, who upholds and supports all things by his will and pleasure.
heir of all things: Possessor and equal partner of all things with the Father.
worlds: That is, whatever has been at any time, is, or shall be.
brightness of his glory: He in whom the glory and majesty of the Father shines, who is otherwise infinite, and cannot be under obligation.
person: His Father's person.
upholding all things by the word: Sustains, defends and cherishes.
when he had by himself purged: The third part of the same proposition: The same Son executed the office of the High Priest in offering up himself, and is our only and most mighty Mediator in heaven.

sat down on the right hand: This shows that the savour of that his sacrifice is not only most acceptable to the Father, but also is everlasting, and furthermore how far this High Priest surpasses all the other high priests.
Being made so much better than: Before he comes to declare the office of Christ, he sets forth the excellency of his person. First of all he shows him to be man, and that in addition he is God also.
name than they: Dignity and honour.

For unto which of the angels: He proves and confirms the dignity of Christ revealed in the flesh, by these six evident testimonies by which it appears that he far surpasses all angels, so much so that he is called both Son, and God in Heb 1:5,6,7,8,10,13.

this day have I begotten thee: The Father begat the Son from everlasting, but that everlasting generation was revealed and represented to the world in his time, and therefore he added this word "Today"

And again: He proves and confirms the dignity of Christ revealed in the flesh, by these six evident testimonies by which it appears that he far surpasses all angels, so much so that he is called both Son, and God in Heb 1:5,6,7,8,10,13.

And: He proves and confirms the dignity of Christ revealed in the flesh, by these six evident testimonies by which it appears that he far surpasses all angels, so much so that he is called both Son, and God in Heb 1:5,6,7,8,10,13.
again: The Lord was not content to have spoken it once, but he repeats it in another place.

And of the angels he saith: He proves and confirms the dignity of Christ revealed in the flesh, by these six evident testimonies by which it appears that he far surpasses all angels, so much so that he is called both Son, and God in Heb 1:5,6,7,8,10,13.
spirits: Cherub, Ps 18:11.
flame of fire: Seraph, Isa 6:2.
throne: The throne is proper for princes and not for servants.
and ever: For everlasting, for this repeating of the word increases the significance of it beyond all measure.
sceptre of righteousness is the sceptre: The government of your kingdom is righteous.
iniquity: This type of speech in which the Jews use contrasting phrases, has great force in it.
anointed thee with the oil of: In that, that the word became flesh, by sending the Holy Spirit on him without measure.
fellows: For he is the head and we are his members.

And: He proves and confirms the dignity of Christ revealed in the flesh, by these six evident testimonies by which it appears that he far surpasses all angels, so much so that he is called both Son, and God in Heb 1:5,6,7,8,10,13.
laid the foundation of the earth: Made the earth firm and sure.

But to which of the angels: He proves and confirms the dignity of Christ revealed in the flesh, by these six evident testimonies by which it appears that he far surpasses all angels, so much so that he is called both Son, and God in Heb 1:5,6,7,8,10,13.
ministering spirits: By that name by which we commonly call princes messengers, he here calls the spirits.
